The source text, verbatim:

# SponsorConnect landing page for plan sponsors

## Business objective
Give MapleSure plan sponsors a single, clear entry page for the SponsorConnect portal so that an HR administrator can find the disability claim submission journey, check a submission's status and reach support in under one minute, without calling the MapleSure service desk.

## Background
Today sponsors land on a generic sign-in screen with no guidance. Service desk logs show that "where do I submit a claim" and "how do I check status" are the two most common sponsor calls. A small, focused landing page is expected to remove most of them.

## Requirements
1. The landing page is served at the portal root ("/") for signed-out and signed-in sponsor users, with the MapleSure brand header and footer.
2. A hero section states what SponsorConnect does in one sentence and shows a primary call to action "Submit a disability claim" that opens the existing claim submission flow (sign-in first if signed out).
3. A secondary call to action "Check submission status" opens the existing submission status page, pre-filtered to the signed-in sponsor's plan.
4. A "How it works" strip shows the three steps: identify the member, complete the claim details and upload documents, receive confirmation and track status.
5. A support panel shows the sponsor service line hours and a link to the sponsor help centre; no phone number is hard-coded in the page, it is read from configuration.
6. The page meets WCAG 2.1 AA: keyboard reachable calls to action, visible focus, colour contrast of at least 4.5:1, and images with alternative text.
7. The page is responsive and usable on a 360px wide mobile viewport as well as desktop.
8. Page views and click-through on each call to action are recorded as analytics events without any member or claim data in the payload.

## Out of scope
Changes to the claim submission form itself, the status page logic, or member-facing pages.
